source.original_text:
Let X be a jointly measurable, strongly progressive process taking values in a compact second-countable pseudometrizable Borel state space S. Let c be a continuous real function of nonnegative time and state. Then the coefficient evaluated along X is strongly progressive. For each finite nonnegative horizon its time section is integrable at every sample. With a finite sample measure, the sample-first product representative belongs to $L^p$ for every exponent p in the extended nonnegative reals.

The sample space carries a finite measure and a filtration indexed by nonnegative time. The horizon T is nonnegative and finite. The integrability exponent p is any extended nonnegative real, including zero and infinity.
The state space S is compact, second countable and pseudometrizable, with its Borel sigma-algebra. The process is jointly measurable and strongly progressive.
The real coefficient c is jointly continuous on nonnegative time times S. The horizon time measure is Lebesgue time restricted to [0,T] on the nonnegative real axis.

b(t,\omega)=c(t,X_t(\omega)),\quad b(\cdot,\omega)\in L^1(\ell_T)\ \ (\forall\omega),\quad [(\omega,t)\mapsto b(t,\omega)]\in L^p(\mu\otimes\ell_T).

  {Ω : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [TopologicalSpace S] [CompactSpace S]
  [TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace S] [SecondCountableTopology S] [MeasurableSpace S] [BorelSpace S]
  {filtration : MeasureTheory.Filtration NNReal inferInstance} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω}
  [MeasureTheory.IsFiniteMeasure μ] (X : NNReal → Ω → S) (hX : Measurable (Function.uncurry X))
  (hProgressive : MeasureTheory.IsStronglyProgressive filtration X) (c : NNReal × S → ℝ) (hc : Continuous c)
  (T : NNReal) (p : ENNReal) :
  have b := fun t ω => c (t, X t ω);
  MeasureTheory.IsStronglyProgressive filtration b ∧
    (∀ (ω : Ω), MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun t => b t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T)) ∧
      MeasureTheory.MemLp (ProgressiveL2.processFunction b) p (ElementaryItoIntegral.processTimeMeasure μ T)

blind_reconstruction.text: Let (Ω,Σ) be a measurable space with a finite measure μ and let S be a compact, pseudometrizable, second-countable topological space equipped with its Borel σ-algebra. Put ℝ₊=[0,∞), with its usual topology and Borel structure, and let (ℱ_a)_{a∈ℝ₊} be a filtration on Ω. Let X:ℝ₊×Ω→S be jointly measurable and strongly progressive for this filtration. Let c:ℝ₊×S→ℝ be continuous for the product topology, and define b(t,ω)=c(t,X(t,ω)). For every T∈ℝ₊ and every p∈[0,∞], all three statements hold. First, b is strongly progressive on all of ℝ₊, meaning that for every a∈ℝ₊ the map (t,ω)↦b(t,ω) on [0,a]×Ω is strongly measurable for the product of the time Borel σ-algebra restricted to [0,a] and ℱ_a. Second, for every ω∈Ω, the real time section t↦b(t,ω) is integrable against λ_T, the pullback by NNReal.toReal of real Lebesgue measure restricted to [0,T]. Third, the map (ω,t)↦b(t,ω) on Ω×ℝ₊ belongs to MemLp with exponent p for the sample-first product measure μ⊗λ_T.

import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.ProgressiveL2
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.Prod

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.CompactProgressiveCoefficients

open Filter MeasureTheory Set TopologicalSpace
open scoped NNReal ENNReal
open ElementaryItoIntegral ProgressiveL2

/-- A continuous scalar coefficient evaluated on a compact-state progressive
process is progressive and has finite horizon integrability. -/
theorem continuous_coefficient_along_compact_process
    {Ω S : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] [TopologicalSpace S] [CompactSpace S]
    [PseudoMetrizableSpace S] [SecondCountableTopology S] [MeasurableSpace S] [BorelSpace S]
    {filtration : Filtration ℝ≥0 (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace Ω)}
    {μ : Measure Ω} [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (X : ℝ≥0 → Ω → S) (hX : Measurable (Function.uncurry X))
    (hProgressive : IsStronglyProgressive filtration X)
    (c : ℝ≥0 × S → ℝ) (hc : Continuous c) (T : ℝ≥0) (p : ℝ≥0∞) :
    let b := fun t ω => c (t, X t ω)
    IsStronglyProgressive filtration b ∧
    (∀ ω, Integrable (fun t => b t ω) (TimeMeasure.upTo T)) ∧
    MemLp (processFunction b) p (processTimeMeasure μ T) := by
  intro b
  have hcompact : IsCompact (Icc (0 : ℝ≥0) T ×ˢ (univ : Set S)) :=
    isCompact_Icc.prod isCompact_univ
  obtain ⟨C, hC⟩ := hcompact.bddAbove_image hc.norm.continuousOn
  have hbound (t : ℝ≥0) (ht : t ≤ T) (ω : Ω) : ‖b t ω‖ ≤ C :=
    hC ⟨(t, X t ω), ⟨⟨bot_le, ht⟩, mem_univ _⟩, rfl⟩
  have htime : ∀ᵐ t ∂TimeMeasure.upTo T, t ≤ T :=
    (TimeMeasure.ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo T).mono fun _ ht => ht.2
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro t
    let _ : MeasurableSpace Ω := filtration t
    exact (hc.measurable.comp
      ((measurable_subtype_coe.comp measurable_fst).prodMk (hProgressive t).measurable)).stronglyMeasurable
  · intro ω
    have hm := hc.measurable.comp (measurable_id.prodMk
      (hX.comp (measurable_id.prodMk (measurable_const (a := ω)))))
    exact Integrable.of_bound hm.aestronglyMeasurable C
      (htime.mono fun t ht => hbound t ht ω)
  · have hXswap : Measurable (fun z : Ω × ℝ≥0 => X z.2 z.1) :=
      hX.comp (measurable_snd.prodMk measurable_fst)
    have hm := hc.measurable.comp (measurable_snd.prodMk hXswap)
    change MemLp (processFunction b) p (μ.prod (TimeMeasure.upTo T))
    exact MemLp.of_bound hm.aestronglyMeasurable C
      ((Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd.ae htime).mono fun z hz => hbound z.2 hz z.1)

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.StochasticProcesses.CompactProgressiveCoefficients

steps.title: Compose on each filtration window
steps.text: At time r the restriction of the process to times t at most r is strongly measurable for the product of the window Borel structure and the sigma-algebra at r. Pair it with the time coordinate, then apply the continuous coefficient.
steps.lean: Use the defining filtration window of IsStronglyProgressive and compose the two measurable coordinates with c.

steps.title: Bound the coefficient uniformly on the horizon
steps.text: Continuity on the compact product of the time interval and state space bounds the absolute value by one deterministic constant. The horizon measure is supported inside that interval.
steps.lean: Apply IsCompact.bddAbove_image to the norm and use ae_mem_Ioc_zero_upTo.

steps.title: Integrate the sections and the product representative
steps.text: Joint measurability gives a measurable time section at every sample. On the product, the same bound holds almost everywhere by projecting onto the time coordinate. Finite measures give the section and product integrability.
steps.lean: Apply Integrable.of_bound for each section and MemLp.of_bound to the sample-first product using Measure.quasiMeasurePreserving_snd.

lesson.lean_statement: The theorem returns strong progressiveness, integrability for each time section, and product MemLp at the requested exponent.
lesson.lean_proof: Combine composition on filtration windows with one compact bound and the finite-measure integrability criteria.
